However, the moment the money changed hands, the script suddenly changed. 

The 'vendor' transformed into a ghost, ghosting phone calls, dodging scheduled meetings, and vanishing into thin air just when post-sale procedures were meant to kick off.

Realising he had been conned, the victim rushed to the police. Kalama Sub-County sleuths immediately swung into action, conducting investigations that uncovered the suspect's true identity as David Maitha, a masquerader who used identity theft as a ticket to a quick, illegal payday.

Maitha is currently cooling his heels in police custody, undergoing processing ahead of his date with the court.

CITY LAWYER ARRESTED FOR FORGERY, ASSAULT ON POLICE OFFICERS

A city lawyer who presented forged documents before the Nairobi Employment and Labour Relations court has today been arrested, following the ODPP's directive to police in Parklands, Nairobi to charge him. The suspect, Benard Odero Okello of Benard Odero & Company Advocates was arrested at his office located at The Westery building in Westlands, Nairobi. 

The ODPP's directive to charge Odero followed painstaking investigations into a complaint filed by three Kenya County Government Workers Union officials, Nairobi Branch who discovered that the suspect had presented a case before the said ELRC at Nairobi Cause No. E068 of 2022, where he presented false documents with forged signatures of the three.

In the case, Odero purported that the complainants had signed a Change of Signatory & Fee Note Agreement, for him to be paid Sh150M upon conclusion of a case in which he alleged to have represented them.

But the complainants disputed having executed or signed the said agreement. The disputed documents, together with specimens of the complainants' known signatures were hence submitted to the forensic document examiner for anlysis.

The forensic report confirmed that, indeed, the documents presented before court by the suspect were forged, supporting the complainants' assertion that the signatures appearing on the disputed documents were not theirs.

Accordingly, a directive was given on September 2, 2026 for the suspect to be charged with two counts of forgery and uttering a false document. 

Odero was summoned to present himself at Parklands Police Station but turned a deaf year, prompting the officers to launch a manhunt for him. He was traced to his office. 

To evade the arrest, the suspect threatened to jump off from the 8th floor window of his office, and when he was finally nabbed, attacked by biting two police officers who were trying to cuff him. 

Consequently, besides the two approved charges with which Odero is faced, additional counts of resisting arrest and assaulting police officers will be preferred.

ARREST OF NOTORIOUS CRIMINAL GANG MEMBER AND RECOVERY OF CANNABIS SATIVA (BHANG), CRUDE WEAPONS, GOVERNMENT STORES AND TACTICAL EQUIPMENT

A multi-agency operation targeting suspected members of criminal gangs and their associates within Kondele, Kisumu County, has resulted in the arrest of a suspected notorious gang member and the recovery of cannabis sativa (bhang), crude weapons, government stores and tactical equipment.

The intelligence-led operation, conducted by officers drawn from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Administration Police Service (APS) and General Service Unit (GSU), intercepted a white Toyota Axio, registration number KCZ 808K, and arrested Franklin Okungu, 34, alias “Ninjaman”, who was aboard the vehicle. The suspect is belived to be a gang member and associate of Oliver Jaoko, alias “Olivetti”.

Following his arrest, the suspect led detectives to his residence in Manyatta area, where a search was conducted. The operation resulted in the recovery of pouches containing arrows, three machetes, a customised club fitted with a metal casing and screw-gear head, two military-pattern jungle ground sheets, a red beret, a tactical shirt, a pair of tactical trousers, a pair of tactical shorts and a black military-style helmet.

Also recovered were 16 Cannabis Sativa-infused cookies (weed cookies), Cannabis Sativa (bhang), a diary containing handwritten entries detailing tactics and techniques, training manuals and other warfare-related material.

The scene was processed and documented by Crime Scene Investigators (CSI) from Nyanza Region, while an inventory of the recovered exhibits was prepared and signed by the suspect.

Preliminary investigations have established that Okungu was an instructor within an outfit known as “American Marines”, reportedly associated with Oliver Jaoko. He is alleged to have trained members of the outfit in the handling of swords, pangas and machetes, as well as karate and other combat techniques.

Investigations have further established that the outfit comprised bouncers and other youths who were allegedly mobilised and hired for various assignments before subsequently evolving into a group known as the “Summit Gang”.

The suspect is being processed for arraignment to face charges including robbery with violence contrary to Section 296(2) of the Penal Code; possession of public stores contrary to Section 324(3) of the Penal Code; possession of property suspected to have been stolen or unlawfully obtained contrary to Section 323 of the Penal Code; possession of narcotic drugs contrary to the applicable provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Control) Act; and participation in organised criminal activity under the applicable law.

A slick counterfeit flour racket that has been flooding Kenyan kitchens with fake maize flour has been dismantled after detectives from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) raided a godown in Canaan area, near Infinity Industrial Park in Kasarani Sub-County. 

Acting on credible intelligence, detectives stormed the premises and unearthed a full-blown repackaging operation, walking away with thousands of counterfeit packets and seven suspects in tow.

Investigations established that the godown had been transformed into a covert factory of fraud, where assorted maize flour brands were being illegally repackaged and redistributed under fake labelling, deceiving unsuspecting consumers into buying products that were not what they claimed to be.

Caught in the dragnet were Felix Kiprop, an employee of SARA Flour Brand; Cynthia Nakoli, a salesperson attached to the same brand; loaders Joseph Kariuki and Victor Omondi Opiyo; driver Daniel Ngugi; and Maria Ngui and Samuel Kimilu, who were all apprehended at the scene as the operation unravelled.

Detectives recovered 3,682 packets of a popular corn maize flour brand, valued at approximately Kshs 312,120, alongside hundreds of packets of three other well-known flour brands, with the combined value of the counterfeit stash running into hundreds of thousands of shillings.

The scene told the story of a well-oiled counterfeiting enterprise: stacks of empty packaging bearing the branding of several genuine maize flour companies, a Hyundai lorry, Registration No. KBR 092K, caught red-handed being loaded with the illicit products, and an array of industrial processing and packaging machinery, weighing equipment, bag-sealing tools, and date and batch marking stamps used to imprint false product information onto fake packaging, all pointing to a syndicate built to deceive on an industrial scale.

Raising particular alarm among investigators was a stash of discarded one-kilogram packaging bearing a close resemblance to a well-known maize flour brand. A representative of the affected brand who rushed to the scene confirmed that while the packaging bore a striking resemblance to his company's branding, it may not have been genuinely manufactured by the company, since the brand does not produce one-kilogram packets, an admission that only deepens suspicion of a deliberate scheme to piggyback on a trusted name.

Representatives of the affected brands have since pledged to present themselves for verification, while the Anti-Counterfeit Authority (ACA) has been roped in to sample the recovered products for further analysis, as the full scale of the racket comes under probe.

The seven suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing pending arraignment, while the recovered items have been detained as exhibits.

The DCI reaffirms its unwavering commitment to combating counterfeit trade and safeguarding Kenyan consumers from fraudulent and potentially harmful products.

The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) has noted claims circulating on social media concerning the death of Dennis Aremo Osiemo while in police custody at Narumoru Police Station. The DCI wishes to place on record the circumstances surrounding his arrest, detention and subsequent death.

Osiemo’s arrest arose from investigations into a case of assault causing actual bodily harm reported at Narumoru Police Station. The complaint related to an incident on 2 July 2026, in which Osiemo, a former farmhand of the complainant, is alleged to have gone to her home, assaulted her and stabbed her several times before fleeing the scene. The complainant reported the matter at Narumoru Police Station and was admitted at Tumutumu Hospital, where she remained for nine days.

The complainant later raised concerns over the handling of the case with the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) in Nanyuki. The ODPP subsequently directed that the matter be taken over by the DCI. The case file was forwarded to the Sub-County Criminal Investigations Officer (SCCIO), Kieni East, on 3 September 2026. Detectives thereafter trailed Osiemo to Kisii, where he was reported to have gone into hiding.

With the assistance of the SCCIO, Masaba North, DCI officers from Kieni East arrested Osiemo in Kisii on 18 September 2026. He was first booked at Keroka Police Station pending collection. He was collected by DCI officers from Kieni East and booked at Narumoru Police Station on 19 September 2026.

On the same day, Osiemo was processed, his statement was recorded, and he was returned to the cells after being observed to be in a normal condition. He was scheduled to be arraigned in court on Monday, 21 September 2026, in connection with the assault case.

On Sunday, 20 September 2026, Osiemo was found hanging from the ventilation grills inside the police cell at Narumoru Police Station. The scene was processed immediately in the presence of officers of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA), senior police officers and a relative. The body was thereafter removed to the Narumoru mortuary pending autopsy.

The investigation into the death has been taken over by IPOA. The DCI will accord the Authority full cooperation.

The DCI extends its deepest condolences to the family, relatives and friends of the late Dennis Aremo Osiemo. It shares in their grief and assures them, and the public, of its commitment to a transparent process aimed at establishing the full circumstances of his death.

The public is urged to rely on verified official information and to await the outcome of the independent investigation, rather than draw conclusions from unverified claims circulating on social media.

Detectives from the Capital Markets Fraud Investigation Unit (CMFIU) have arrested two women linked to Quant Vest Stock Exchange (QVSE), also known as Global Investment Group, an entity suspected of operating an unlicensed investment scheme in Kenya.

The arrests followed intelligence received by the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) indicating that the entity was allegedly operating a fraudulent pyramid scheme in which participants were incentivised to recruit new members in exchange for bonuses and other financial rewards.

Preliminary investigations established that the scheme appeared to rely largely on the continuous recruitment of new participants rather than identifiable legitimate investment or business activities.

Investigations further revealed that funds received from investors were allegedly converted into virtual assets and transferred to unidentified recipients, complicating efforts to trace the movement of the money and establish its ultimate beneficiaries.

The scheme is also believed to have mounted an aggressive recruitment drive through physical promotional campaigns on social media platforms, particularly TikTok and Bon Chat. 

Investigators established that numerous prospective investors were targeted in Machakos, Kitui and Makindu, where promotional meetings were reportedly organised at predetermined locations to attract new members.

Following a thorough investigation, CMFIU detectives arrested Ruth Mueni Kimeu, believed to be the QVSE representative for Machakos County, and Mary Katuma Mwangangi, the entity’s representative in Kitui County.

The two suspects were yesterday, 23rd September 2026, arraigned before the Kilimani Chief Magistrate’s Court, where they faced charges of carrying out the business of a collective investment scheme and fraudulently inducing members of the public to trade in securities by publishing false and misleading information.

They pleaded not guilty to the charges and were each released on a bond of Sh200,000, as investigations and the court process continue.

The DCI cautions members of the public against entrusting their hard-earned money to unlicensed investment schemes or being lured by promises of quick returns. Members of the public are encouraged to verify the licensing status of investment entities with the relevant regulatory authorities before committing their funds.

A suspect accused of forging company records to facilitate the unlawful removal of a director from two companies has been arraigned before a Milimani court, where he faced 12 counts of making and uttering false documents.

Mandeep Singh Channa was arrested by detectives from the DCI Headquarters yesterday September 24, 2026, following investigations into allegations that fraudulent changes were effected at the Business Registration Services, resulting in the purported removal of a director of Channa Construction Ltd and Channa Investment Ltd.

The matter was reported to DCI Headquarters after the complainant, who is a director in the two companies, discovered that he had allegedly been removed from their directorship without his knowledge or consent.

A subsequent search through the e-Citizen platform unearthed documents that raised further suspicion, including purported Annual General Meeting (AGM) minutes and an affidavit bearing his alleged signature, indicating that he had forfeited his shareholding and resigned as a director of both companies.

The complainant, however, denied signing the documents or taking any steps to relinquish his shareholding and directorship, prompting investigations by detectives.

Upon conclusion of investigations, the  case file was forwarded to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) for review. Upon perusal, the ODPP directed that Channa be charged with offences of making a false document and uttering a false document.

Following his arrest, the suspect was today, September 25, 2026, presented before Milimani Chief Magistrate’s Court No. 1 where he faced 12 counts and pleaded not guilty to all the charges.

The court granted him a bond of Sh500,000 with a similar surety, or an alternative cash bail of Sh300,000. Among the bond conditions, the suspect was directed to deposit his passport in court.

The case will be mentioned on October 8, 2026.

ARREST OF A MURDER SUSPECT

Detectives in Meru County have arrested a prime suspect in connection with the murder of 65-year-old Evelyne Mukiri Mbaabu, who was fatally attacked at her home in Kithoka, Imenti East Sub-county, on August 7, 2026.

The elderly woman was preparing supper with her 13-year-old grandson when an unknown man entered the compound and proceeded to the kitchen, where he asked for drinking water. Moments later, the boy heard his grandmother scream for help. He rushed to the kitchen, only to find her lying in a pool of blood, before the assailant turned on him, striking him on the hand with a panga before fleeing.

The victim was rushed to Grace Park Hospital, where she was pronounced dead on arrival.

Following weeks of forensic analysis and intelligence-led investigations by detectives from the CCIO’s Office and DCI Imenti North, the prime suspect, Solomon Kathurima Kairemia, was traced and arrested on September 21, 2026.

By the time detectives caught up with him, Kairemia had abandoned his house and resorted to spending nights hiding in nearby thickets, just a few metres from his residence.

During the arrest, detectives recovered a blood-stained panga, believed to have been used in the fatal attack. The weapon was secured as an exhibit for further forensic examination.

A police identification parade was subsequently conducted, during which Kairemia was positively identified as the man behind the fatal attack.

The suspect was presented before the Meru Law Courts, where investigators obtained a 14-day custodial order to allow them to complete the ongoing investigations.

The DCI extends its condolences to the family, friends and relatives of Evelyne Mukiri Mbaabu and remains committed to pursuing every available lead to establish the motive and circumstances surrounding her murder, and ensure that all those found culpable are brought to justice.

14 HELD AS DCI BUST SUSPECTED COUNTERFEIT CURRENCY OPERATION IN NAIROBI

DCI detectives based at the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) have arrested 14 suspects, among them three serving police officers and several foreign nationals, following a raid on a warehouse in the Vision Plaza Industrial Area, Nairobi, where suspected counterfeit US currency, fake gold bars and materials believed to be used in the production of counterfeit currency were recovered.

The operation, mounted on October 1, 2026, followed a complaint by a US national, Alkhalifi Ibrahim Hassan, and recorded at the JKIA Police Station.

The suspects, comprising Kenyan and foreign nationals from Nigeria, Cameroon and Sudan, as well as three police officers attached to the Security of Government Buildings (SGB), Uhuru Camp, were arrested after DCI officers searched the warehouse located behind Vision Plaza. Two officers were armed with Beretta pistols whereas their other accomplice was armed with a Chalbi pistol. 

The suspects are, Anthony Oyieka Namani- Nigerian, Soulemanou- Cameroonian, Abbas Ibrahim Mohamed- Sudanese, George Kinyanjui, Geofrey Omondi Juma, William Kimolo, Solomon Ndeda, Raphael Wayaya, Kevin Barasa, Erick Honla, Maureen Ogany, Cpl Joseph Otenyo Okimba, APC Douglas O. Odira and APC Felix Oyawa Odhiambo

A total of 31 sealed black pallets were recovered. Further scrutiny established that three of the pallets contained 156 bundles of US$100 notes suspected to be counterfeit, while the remaining pallets contained cement.

A murder suspect who went on the run after the brutal killing of a Form Four student in Molo has been arrested, following a sustained manhunt by detectives.

The suspect, Walter Kipkoech, 23, was traced to a hideout in Lagwenda village, Kuresoi North, where detectives from Molo, alongside their counterparts from the Crime Research and Intelligence Bureau (CRIB) at the Regional Criminal Investigations Headquarters, Rift Valley, smoked him out of his hideout.

Kipkoech had reportedly fled immediately after the killing of 18-year-old Joy Wangui, a Form Four student at Molo Secondary School, whose lifeless body was discovered inside a house in Kiambaa area, Moto Location.

Her brother, who had briefly left home for a nearby shop, returned to a horrifying scene: his sister lying in a pool of blood in the kitchen, her head severed from the body.

The responding detectives found the murder weapon, an axe, a panga and two knives, all bearing bloodstains, near the body.

The deceased’s head was later discovered in the corridor, where a message had allegedly been scrawled on the wall using blood: “I love you Joy but never cheat, am sorry.”

Preliminary investigations established that Kipkoech was the deceased’s boyfriend, as detectives pursued a possible relationship dispute as the motive for the killing.

When the long arm of the law finally caught up with him, Kipkoech was wearing a blood-stained boxer, a white T-shirt bearing the deceased’s name at the hem, and black jeans with visible dry blood stains.

The suspect was escorted to Molo Police Station, where he is undergoing processing pending arraignment, as detectives continue with investigations as they piece together the events leading to the horrific killing.

The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) conveys its deepest condolences to the family, relatives and friends of the late Joy Wangui, whose life was tragically cut short. OPERATION USALAMA XII: MULTI-AGENCY CRACKDOWN YIELDS KSH 62.7 MILLION IN SUSPECTED CONTRABAND

The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), in collaboration with INTERPOL and other law enforcement and regulatory agencies, have concluded a three-day nationwide multi-agency operation targeting counterfeit goods, illicit alcohol, soft drinks, smuggled cigarettes, self-care products, falsified pharmaceuticals, human trafficking and wildlife-related crimes.

Dubbed Operation Usalama XII, the intelligence-led exercise covered Nairobi, Central, Coast, Rift Valley, Eastern, Nyanza and Western regions, bringing together the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), Anti-Counterfeit Authority (ACA), Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS), Transnational Organized Crime Unit (TOCU), Anti-Human Trafficking and Child Protection Unit (AHTCPU), National Anti-Narcotic Investigations Bureau (NANIB), Pharmacy and Poisons Board, brand owners and local police units.

The three-day operation that was coordinated by the National Central Bureau [NCB] and Director Operations DCI HQs recorded 29 arrests, seizures of suspected counterfeit and contraband goods valued at over KSh 62.7 million, 198 motor vehicle checks against INTERPOL databases, seven suspected victims of trafficking rescued and 85 Kenyan passports recovered from a suspected illegal recruitment agency.

In Nairobi, detectives recovered suspected counterfeit consumer goods, electrical accessories and automotive components worth millions of shillings. The seizures included 3,991-suspected counterfeit Samsung and iPhone adapters, 1,963 football jerseys and Adidas balls, beauty products, vehicle spareparts and lubricants. Officers also recovered suspected falsified pharmaceuticals and diverted public medical supplies from an unlicensed clinic in Kayole, while NANIB detectives seized several bottles of products suspected to contain narcotic or psychotropic substances from a pharmacy in Eastleigh for further analysis.

The operation also targeted suspects in human trafficking and exploitation. In Westlands, detectives arrested a suspect at a recruitment agency allegedly operating without the requisite license, recovering 85 Kenyan passports, work visas and employment contracts. In Roysambu, three girls were rescued from suspected sexual exploitation, while a separate operation in Gilgil intercepted four Somali nationals suspected to be trafficking victims, including two minors.

In Nakuru, officers arrested a suspect transporting 90,000 sticks of suspected smuggled cigarettes valued at approximately KSh 2 million and recovered counterfeit excise stamps. Other operations led to arrests and seizures of counterfeit and unmarked alcoholic beverages in Central and Nyanza regions, alongside the recovery of suspected counterfeit mobile phones, storage devices and footwear.

TWO SUSPECTS ARRESTED OVER KSH 530,000 CHICKS SUPPLY FRAUD

Two suspects have been arrested in connection with Ksh 530,000 fraud involving the supply of 7,500 chicks valued at Ksh 1,387,500.

The suspects, identified as Marysella Naswa Kanda and Angela Kendi have been arraigned before the Chief Magistrate’s Court in Ngong, where they faced a charge of conspiracy to defraud, contrary to Section 317 of the Penal Code. 

The court granted them cash bail of Ksh 250,000 each or an alternative bond of Ksh 300,000, with the case scheduled for mention on 9th November 2026.

Investigations commenced after the complainant reported the fraud at Kiserian Police Station. The complainant had ordered 7,500 chicks but  received none despite making payments totalling Ksh 530,000.

According to the complaint, the first payment of Ksh 350,000 was deposited into a Co-operative Bank account operated under Japlead Global Feed, reportedly owned by Marysella, on 13th September 2026. A further Ksh 180,000 was deposited into the same account on 16th September 2026 after the complainant was promised a 'before shedule' delivery. However, the chicks were never delivered.

Following the report, officers from Kiserian Police Station launched investigations and conducted an undercover operation, posing as prospective clients seeking to order chicks. OPERATION CARBACK II: MULTI-AGENCY CRACKDOWN UNCOVERS LUXURY VEHICLE STOLEN IN THE UK

A major breakthrough in the fight against transnational motor vehicle crime has seen detectives recover a luxury vehicle stolen in the United Kingdom, in a week-long, multi-agency crackdown dubbed Operation Carback II, targeting local and transnational motor vehicle theft syndicates.

The operation, which concluded yesterday, was spearheaded by the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), through its INTERPOL National Central Bureau in Nairobi (NCB-Nairobi) and the Operations Directorate, in collaboration with other DCI directorates and key national law enforcement and regulatory agencies.

Kenya joined other INTERPOL member countries in the simultaneous global operation, coordinated under Project Drive Out in collaboration with the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol). The initiative aimed to disrupt organised motor vehicle crime networks, identify and recover stolen vehicles and vehicle parts, and strengthen cross-border law enforcement cooperation.

The multi-agency team brought together the National Transport and Safety Authority (NTSA), Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP), Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS), Kenya Police Service and Administration Police Service.

Building on the success of a similar operation conducted in 2024, Operation Carback II delivered a nationwide enforcement sweep, with detectives physically inspecting more than 1,800 vehicles and checking over 260,000 vehicles against the INTERPOL database.

The teams fanned out across Nairobi, Eastern, Central, Nyanza, Western, Coast and Rift Valley regions, targeting motor vehicle yards, showrooms, spare-parts shops, garages, motor vehicle bazaars and highway checkpoints.

Along Nairobi County’s Northern Bypass, detectives raided a motor vehicle yard and recovered a grey Land Rover Discovery bearing registration number KCY 001J. A check against the INTERPOL database established that the vehicle had been reported stolen in the United Kingdom. It was subsequently impounded and escorted to DCI Headquarters for further processing and investigations.

In Thika West Sub-County, detectives uncovered a white Mercedes-Benz Kompressor fitted with registration number KBZ 325J, which belongs to an orange Suzuki station wagon. The discovery raised questions about the vehicle’s identity and registration, prompting further investigations by the Sub-County Criminal Investigations Officer.

Meanwhile, in Embakasi, detectives recovered a forklift bearing registration number KAD 132K, which was found to belong to a crawler. The discovery of an obliterated chassis number raised further suspicion, leading to the referral of the matter to DCI Embakasi for further investigations and appropriate action.

These findings underscore the critical role of intelligence-led operations, coordinated enforcement and international information-sharing in detecting, disrupting and dismantling motor vehicle theft syndicates operating within Kenya and across international borders.

The DCI remains steadfast in its commitment to working with national, regional and international partners to combat motor vehicle theft, recover stolen property and bring those involved in these criminal networks to justice.

 “Inauma lakini itabidi mzoee.” “Just a normal Tuesday.” “Sherehe haitaki hasira.” Filter zimefanya overtime, and pengtings were sliding into DMs faster than a kienyeji Jogoo running away from Christmas knife.

Behind the glamorous posts, private chats and big promises were luring damsels into Vinnie’s soft-life kingdom. Simu zinazimwa, locations zinapotea, and suddenly families are asking, “Where are our daughters?”

Pay up or face the consequences. The girls who had come for luxury were now running “small errands” to repay what had been spent on them.

Soft life ikageuka kazi!

Vinnie had turned Kanairo into his own Strait of Hormuz. Keja mob kwa riba, lakini kwa ground ni tenant wa BnBs! Every other week, a new apartment. The pengtings thought he owned half of Kanairo. Kumbe landlord alikuwa anangoja rent kama wengine!

Then came the night the soft-life empire came tumbling down. Vanessa (Pedi) was sent on one of Vinnie’s “small errands,” delivering a package to a busy Westy local hangout, unaware that our boys were undercover among the revellers. 

She walked in looking like an influencer on a sponsored night out, Unyunyu ikitangaza arrival kabla afike kwa counter. The moment she handed over the package, our boys struck. The client developed instant amnesia, pretending hajui Vanessa tangu creation. Wapi! Within minutes, the package was secured, and Vanessa was joining our boys for a very different kind of stay.

But her arrest was only the beginning. The Disiyai had been following leads on missing young women, and the investigation was now connecting the dots. Girls who had switched off their phones and vanished into temporary apartments started reappearing in statements. Families who had been asking, “Where are our daughters?” finally had a name and a face to attach to the silence. 

The pattern was becoming disturbing: glamorous posts, private promises, switched-off phones, ever-changing addresses and young women being recruited while the outside world remained clueless.

Vinnie, dressed in style ya Ngoma ya Matata na Sauti, was cornered in one of his hideouts by our sleuths. 

 Suddenly, all that big vocabulary turned into lugha ya taifa. “Mangapi, wakuu?” His sponsors, allegedly trying to cross into a neighbouring country, were also nabbed and are now enjoying ugali served with bean stew and few leafy greens while they await the court’s decision.

You know a friend who knows a friend, or have a family member who suddenly goes quiet and starts talking about “big opportunities”? Ask questions before the questions start asking for you.

DCI Welcomes Conviction of Paul Mackenzie and 28 Co-Accused in Shakahola Massacre

The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) welcomes the landmark judgment delivered today by the Mombasa High Court, in which Lady Justice Diana Kavedza- Mochache convicted controversial preacher Paul Nthenge Mackenzie and 28 co-accused over the deaths of 191 people, including 190 children, in the Shakahola massacre in Kilifi County.

In her judgment, Justice Kavedza found that the deaths resulted from an organised system in which religious teachings and a structured hierarchy were used to direct and enforce deadly fasting. Followers were instructed to relocate to Shakahola, where fasting was imposed in stages, beginning with children. Guards allegedly prevented followers from escaping the deadly practice.

The conviction follows an extensive investigation and prosecution supported by evidence from 123 witnesses, including child victims. The evidence was further corroborated by digital recordings, forensic and medical reports, DNA analysis, physical exhibits and expert testimony. Crime scene investigations also documented bodies exhumed from homesteads and mass graves.

Medical evidence established that 76 of the victims died from starvation, among other causes of death established through 190 postmortem examinations.

The court further found that Good News International Church, founded by Mackenzie in 2010, operated as a cult. The church reportedly preached the imminent end of the world, discouraged access to medicine and education, isolated followers and promoted extreme fasting as a means of attaining heaven.

In acknowledging the DCI's role, the court commended investigators for their meticulous work in scene documentation, exhumations, forensic pathology and evidence preservation. It noted that these efforts laid a firm foundation for the administration of justice.

The DCI welcomes the judgment as a significant milestone in the pursuit of justice for the victims and their families, underscoring the importance of thorough investigations, forensic expertise and evidence-led prosecutions in holding those responsible for serious crimes accountable.

An investigation into alleged insider fraud, digital manipulation and suspicious financial transactions has led to the arrest and arraignment of a former Credit Control Officer at an insurance company, Bernard Kariuki Ngugi, over the suspected theft of Sh89,579,274 from his former employer.

Investigations by detectives from the Banking Fraud Investigations Unit (BFIU) established that between 2018 and November 2025, the suspect exploited his privileged access to the company’s financial systems to orchestrate the diversion of millions of shillings through three companies: Auris General Merchants Ltd, Donbitz Global Limited and Pedram Global Limited.

The three entities, according to investigators, had no legitimate business relationship with the insurance company and were not entitled to receive the payments, raising red flags over how they found their way into the company’s payment system.

Investigators established that the scheme involved manipulating the company’s financial systems to introduce the three companies into the payment chain, paving the way for the diversion of corporate funds. 

It was established that, Sh35.27 million was channelled through Auris General Merchants Ltd, Sh32.68 million through Donbitz Global Limited and a further Sh21.63 million through Pedram Global Limited. 

Investigators also established that withdrawals and transfers were made in circumstances designed to obscure the origin and movement of the funds.

With the evidence assembled, the investigation file was forwarded to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP), which concurred with the investigators’ recommendation to charge the suspect with theft by servant, money laundering and other related offences.

The suspect was subsequently trailed and arrested in Nairobi before being arraigned at the Milimani Law Courts today October 23, 2026. He pleaded not guilty to all the charges and was released on a bond of Sh2 million, with an alternative cash bail of Sh800,000.

The case is scheduled for a pre-trial mention on November 10, 2026.

ARREST OF SUSPECT OVER  ONLINE INCITEMENT 

A joint team of detectives from DCI Headquarters Operations Action Team (OAT) and Crime Research and Intelligence Bureau (CRIB) has arrested Festus Kipkirui, alias Festoo, who is suspected of operating a Facebook page under the pseudonym Kipz Prince en Narok that is under investigation over reports of online incitement.

The suspect was arrested in Mararianda, Narok East, Narok County. He is undergoing police processing ahead of his anticipated arraignment in court to face relevant charges.

The arrest underscores the Directorate of Criminal Investigations’ (DCI) commitment to addressing offences that threaten national cohesion and peaceful coexistence.

The DCI urges members of the public to exercise responsibility in their online communications and refrain from content that promotes hatred, division or incitement.
